In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the post-Newtonian models currently available are not adequate for the detection of neutron-star–back-hole binary inspirals.

, while the post-Newtonian approximation to the gravitational waveforms of neutron-star– black-hole binaries is not accurate enough to be used for detection purposes, the current level of accuracy is sufficient to provide useful information about the binary parameters, such as the mass ratio, and to provide a rough estimate of the spin of the compact objects.
, at this stage, it is not clear which of the existing approximants is more appropriate for the analysis of data from neutron-star–black hole binary inspirals.

, the current post-Newtonian models are inadequate to model the gravitational-wave signals from neutron-star–black hole binaries, and new models are needed to model these signals

, in the case of neutron star–black hole binaries, the post-Newtonian approximation is no longer sufficient for accurate modeling of the gravitational waves.
